findings.claim: Sebrae reports 22,869 startups mapped through December 2025; this is the report's mapped universe, not a verified census of all eligible Brazilian startups.
ABStartups' 2025 study analyses self-declared information from 3,650 mapped active startups, collected July–September 2025 across 424 cities.
findings.universe: respondents / existing registry updates plus new registrations

findings.claim: Sebrae describes a predominance of B2B and SaaS, with 51.8% reporting AI in products or operations. These source-universe characteristics guide sampling, not market-share conclusions.
The Sebrae 2025 municipal table places São Paulo first, followed by Florianópolis, Rio de Janeiro, Recife, Fortaleza, Brasília, Belo Horizonte, Curitiba, Porto Alegre and Teresina.
findings.interpretation: mapped-population order only; avoid presenting as a universal ecosystem-quality ranking

findings.claim: Inova Unicamp's 2026 voluntary registry reports 2,055 cumulative company registrations and 1,624 active firms. The universe includes alumni-founded companies and spin-offs across Brazil and abroad, not just Campinas startups.
findings.universe: active firms in voluntary university-affiliated registry

findings.claim: San Pedro Valley identifies itself as a founder-created Belo Horizonte community originating in the São Pedro neighbourhood and links a self-registration startup directory.

Curitiba's 2025 retrospective connects the Vale do Pinhão network, Worktiba residency, Pinhão Hub and investment/funding actors. Its stated 670 startups is a municipal universe distinct from Sebrae's mapped count.
ACATE describes regional poles and the MIDIHUB incubator network using MIDITEC methods. Its broader technology-industry measures should not be relabelled startup totals.
Tecnopuc organises sector hubs including agrifood, education, finance, creative industry, AI, mobility and health. Its text-rendered +0 counters are unavailable observations, not zeros.

Porto Digital integrates startups, established companies, universities and public actors in Recife, spanning IT, digital communication, automation, AI and creative activity. Its 541 displayed firms are broader than startups.

COPPE/UFRJ's incubator lists technology-based domains including health/biotech, energy, sustainability, smart cities, oil/gas, naval industry and advanced manufacturing, providing a deep-tech discovery route.
Ceará's Corredores Digitais 2026 call separated Bora Criar for early ideas from Bora Crescer for operating businesses. Its stated June 8 deadline is historical by this checkpoint.
findings.freshness_note: Earlier successful page read; final recheck timed out. Does not establish current intake status.

findings.claim: CERTI describes Jornada Amazônia as a startup-development pathway connecting forest-conservation-oriented businesses to technical support, markets and investment.

The BNDES Garagem 2026 application page states intake October 28–November 30, up to 100 selections, creation and traction modules, and socioenvironmental impact themes. This does not confer an individual eligibility determination.
PIPE provides non-repayable innovation-research support for small companies. The rules effective September 15 2026 require at most 250 employees and a real headquarters or research unit in São Paulo.

Embrapii/Sebrae offers technical and financial R&D support; its page advertises coverage up to 90% under project-dependent conditions and identifies Sebrae support for annual revenue up to BRL 4.8 million.

Finep's current opportunity portal separates credit, non-repayable support and indirect investment. The Finep Startup page states continuous intake suspended from June 30 2025, so older rolling-intake descriptions are stale.

The 2026 InovAtiva de Impacto announcement reports 72 selected ventures and limits that edition to Alagoas, Ceará, Espírito Santo, Pará, Pernambuco and Rio Grande do Norte. Programme-wide older eligibility must not override this edition.

Anjos do Brasil reports a 2025 angel-investment estimate of BRL 919 million and 8,044 investors in its June 2026 publication. These survey estimates are ecosystem context, not startup-level funding events.
ABVCAP/TTR's 2025 VC section counts investments in Brazilian companies initiated during the period, completed or ongoing; amount totals use non-confidential values and exclude angel investments.

Kaszek offers country-HQ, sector and active/exit filters; monashees shows initial investment labels and headquarters; Canary exposes selected announcements; Latitud exposes sector/market filters. These are discovery routes requiring company- and event-level review.
WOW describes national remote-compatible startup acceleration supported by an angel-investor network. Its Batch 36 banner was open at retrieval, but an exact closing date was not verified.
ACE's Digital Acceleration Turma 14 targets Espírito Santo and states an October 17 2026 deadline; that call is historical at this checkpoint despite retained open-application wording.

BNDES Garagem's directory displays 398 results but exposes only 12 cards before a Load more button in the retrieved text. No pagination completion, eligible denominator or 398 verified-company claim is made.
The Sebrae observatory lists Brazil, Northeast, Amazônia Legal, regional and deep-tech reports as discovery routes; linked reports and their licensing/access conditions require separate review.
